page_placements.theme: Loss bumps and abrupt ICL gains without induction heads

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on toy non-ergodic data that bear on induction-head formation and training-loss transitions, but does not report the original study's detailed mechanism or measurement procedure.
record.gate_note: The post reports preliminary induction-head evidence and loss transitions in toy-network experiments, plus a coin-source experiment on in-context loss. It does not report the specific previous-token-head composition or copy-pattern measurements, or an explicit alignment between induction-head formation, an ICL gain, and a loss bump. Its discussion of LLM power-law loss and the cited Anthropic results does not give separate model-level results here.
record.test_reason: The post briefly reports the authors' own experiments training transformers and RNNs on toy non-ergodic data. They observed phase transitions in training loss, which they call preliminary evidence of induction-head formation. They also report a coin-source experiment where in-context loss depends on the training mixture. This is a new data setting with results bearing on V2 and V5, but the evidence is preliminary, qualitative and gives no numbers.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that in-context learning emerges from belief updating over non-Markovian, non-ergodic training data, and that induction heads are a natural solution to source disambiguation. Because RNNs also showed loss phase transitions, they suggest induction heads are one instance of a broader class of source-disambiguation or generalization mechanisms. They describe the induction-head evidence as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: The post summarizes toy non-ergodic data experiments and reports preliminary head-formation and loss-transition evidence; it does not specify the original study's detailed procedure or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported coin-source experiment says the transient loss increase and synchronization speed vary with the number of coin sources.

fits_no_version.finding: RNNs trained on the same toy non-ergodic data also show training-loss phase transitions, though they cannot form attention-based induction heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss phase transitions tied to in-context source disambiguation arise in non-attention architectures, so a loss bump alone is not diagnostic of induction heads.

fits_no_version.finding: In-context loss converges to the data generator's myopic entropy, and non-ergodic training data yields power-law decay of in-context loss (theory plus toy experiments).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-ergodic, hierarchical source structure in training data is sufficient for power-law in-context loss.

record.problems: The results are described as preliminary, with no model names, sizes, numerical measurements, uncertainty estimates, or detailed head-formation criteria. The post does not report whether head formation, ICL improvement, and the loss transition coincide in time.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported result rows were left out. Theoretical claims and findings attributed to cited work were not recorded as experimental rows.

untested.parts: Composition with a previous-token head and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying mechanism are not measured.
Head formation measured directly; narrowness and early timing of the window; coincidence with an in-context-learning gain.
No large-model test of induction heads as the mechanism behind most in-context learning.
No comparison of induction heads across model families, sizes or training runs.
Whether and when induction heads form as a function of data properties is not shown with head measures. Only in-context loss dynamics versus number of sources is reported.

missing.what: Experimental claim that in-context loss converges to myopic entropy and follows power-law decay under non-ergodic data. It is reported qualitatively with no row; it is relevant context for V5 and for in-context learning not tied to induction heads.
missing.locator: Next-Token Pretraining Implies In-Context Learning section

record.verdict_notes: This is a lab progress-report blog post summarizing arXiv:2505.18373. The full paper may contain the actual head-level analyses and numbers and should be read for a firmer verdict. Here every result is qualitative, with no model sizes, metrics or uncertainty. The RNN finding implicitly qualifies the use of loss bumps as a signature of induction-head formation (V2), but the post gives no data that tests V2's head–loss coincidence directly.

versions.untested_parts: The composition with a previous-token head and implementation of the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying pattern are not tested.
The post does not establish that formation is abrupt within a narrow early-training window or that it occurs at the same point as an ICL gain and a loss bump.
No test of induction heads as the mechanism behind most ICL in large transformers is reported.
The post does not compare induction-head behaviour across model families, sizes, or training runs. Its RNN result concerns a broader mechanism, not induction heads.
The reported data-dependence result concerns a toy coin-source setting; the post does not systematically vary other training-data properties or training setups.
No comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms for few-shot task learning is reported.
The post does not test whether induction-head formation consists of separate sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.measure: Transient in-context loss and synchronization to the fair-coin loss
rows.value: The transient loss increase is worse and synchronization to the 1-bit fair-coin loss is slower as the number of trained-on coins increases.
rows.note: The post attributes this trend to theory and experiments but does not identify the model or give numerical results for the comparison.
rows.check: This measures in-context loss dynamics as a function of how many training sources (coins) there are. That is in-context learning behaviour depending on training data, not induction-head formation. The architecture is not stated and no numbers are given.
